correctness.rationale: The five-coordinate parity-lifted construction has exactly 32 distinct codewords; its two binary group patterns have no proper prefix/suffix match and parity excludes Hamming distance one. For the upper bound, length-one overlap exclusion forces disjoint start/end symbol sets; word reversal reduces every case to a first-symbol alphabet of size 1 or 2. Exhaustive independent regeneration gives exactly 180 and 240 individually unbordered candidate words, respectively. Bundled 32-clique covers in each pairwise-conflict graph cover every candidate; every clique edge and all coverage are checked by both a string-based and an independently implemented base-four integer-based verifier. Thus 32 is a universal bound in the exact finite scope. The single-template upper bound 27 follows from two puncturing injections, with equality from a ternary checksum. All calculations are reproduced from package-relative files; there is no inference from partial searches to a universal conclusion.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact simultaneous non-overlap and minimum Hamming-distance-two maximum 32 for four symbols and length five, together with the strict single-template ceiling 27. Earlier work defines the same combined coding constraints and gives general bounds/constructions, while later exact length-five results are unrestricted by Hamming distance. The accessible relevant primary full texts and public mathematical record do not state or imply the sharp exact 32. A relevant 2025 restricted-overlap paper could not be inspected in its complete text, so unindexed duplication remains a genuine documented risk. This is a finite priority judgment, not a proof that no unindexed result exists.
residual_risks: The full Wang–Fang–Feng 2025 paper was unavailable for decisive inspection; an otherwise unstated exact four-symbol case could exist in its appendices.

value.rationale: The coding question couples two separately motivated, classical requirements: synchronization across word boundaries and guaranteed single-substitution detection over a natural four-letter alphabet. The exact answer 32 is not a passive recomputation of unrestricted S(4,5)=81. The sharp certificate proves a real nontrivial Hamming-constrained gap, and the 32-word dual-template construction exceeds the best 27-word realization in any single I^4J family by 5. Determining this natural small alphabet/length boundary gives a reusable exact design benchmark, though no claim of a general coding theorem is made.
